precepts.text: Abedmelech's deliverance is tied back to the moment the king commanded him to lift Jeremiah out of the miry dungeon before he perished.
precepts.point: But in that day He will deliver Abedmelech, who shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, and shall not fall by the sword, because he has put his trust in the Most High; the Most High deals with the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah, sent to take the prophet up out of the dungeon before he died.
precepts.why:
The Lord deals with Abedmelech the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah. In the chapter before: “Then the king commanded Ebed–melech the Ethiopian, saying, Take from hence thirty men with thee, and take up Jeremiah the prophet out of the dungeon, before he die.”

Abedmelech was sent to take the prophet up out of the miry dungeon before he perished. So while Jeremiah is still shut up in the court of the prison, the word comes for the Ethiopian: the Lord will bring his words upon the city for evil, but in that day he will deliver Abedmelech; he shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, nor fall by the sword, because he put his trust in the Lord. His deliverance is tied back to the moment the king commanded him to lift Jeremiah out.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why:
This shows a little of what America did to us. “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem”, who said raze it, “even to the foundation thereof.” Edom assisted the Babylonians in destroying Jerusalem. Remember, Edom is the Caucasian race.

“O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed.” Edom stood with Babylon when Jerusalem was burned and its walls broken down, and the scripture says that daughter of Babylon is to be destroyed. What Edom did in the day of Jerusalem is what Edom did to our people again in America.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why: Our people did not believe this would happen, but it took place, and it is the same thing that happened to our people in the 1600s. God says “I will make this proverb to cease”, and “The days are at hand, and the effect of every vision”: what the prophets saw was coming to pass. “There shall be no more any vain vision” within the house of Israel.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why:
This is the proverb God made to cease: “The days are prolonged, and every vision faileth.” A lot of Israelites didn’t believe it. They didn’t believe Moses: ‘no, that’s not gonna happen, that’s gonna fail, that’s not gonna take place.’ But it did.

The proof is the condition of our people today. We’re wasted, we’re destroyed, because we don’t even remember our true heritage.

moments.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: In the ninth year of Zedekiah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar and all his army come against Jerusalem and besiege it, and in the eleventh year, the fourth month, the ninth day, the city is broken up.

The princes of the king of Babylon come in and sit in the middle gate; when Zedekiah and the men of war see them, they flee by night by the way of the king's garden through the gate between the two walls toward the plain.

The Chaldean army pursues and overtakes Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho, and they bring him up to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where the king of Babylon slays Zedekiah's sons and all the nobles of Judah before his eyes, then puts out Zedekiah's eyes, binds him with chains for Babylon, and burns the king's house and the houses of the people, breaking down the walls of Jerusalem.

Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carries away captive to Babylon the remnant of the people that remained in the city, those who fell away to him, and the rest, but leaves the poor of the people who had nothing in the land of Judah and gives them vineyards and fields.
Nebuchadnezzar gives charge concerning Jeremiah that he be taken, looked to well, and done no harm, but treated as he himself shall say.
The princes of Babylon send and take Jeremiah out of the court of the prison and commit him to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to carry him home, so he dwells among the people.

While Jeremiah is still shut up in the court of the prison, the word of the Most High comes to him for Abedmelech the Ethiopian, declaring that He will bring His words upon this city for evil and not for good, and they shall be accomplished in that day.

But in that day He will deliver Abedmelech, who shall not be given into the hand of the men he is afraid of, and shall not fall by the sword, because he has put his trust in the Most High; the Most High deals with the Ethiopian because he was used to help Jeremiah, sent to take the prophet up out of the dungeon before he died.
Chapter 39 is Jerusalem destroyed: Babylon annihilates Jerusalem. This is the final destruction, and the final destruction means the destruction of the temple.

Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came with all his army against Jerusalem, “and they besieged it.” When you read it, they besieged Jerusalem between eighteen and thirty months. That’s damn near two years, no food, no water. That’s where you get the Book of Lamentations, and that’s where you get Deuteronomy 28 being fulfilled on our people: people eating each other.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: “The city was broken up.” Imagine the siege: no food for a year, a year and a half, two years. You can say ‘I would never eat somebody’, but try having no food for a year and a half. This is what a lot of Israelites were doing, eating each other. Could you imagine looking at your own child as a piece of chicken? This is what our people came down to: they started to eat the flesh of their own children, husbands eating their wives.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: Zedekiah tried to run. He saw the princes of Babylon in the gate and fled with the men of war “out of the city by night”, but the Chaldeans “overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.” The map of the deportations of the Jews shows it: Nebuchadnezzar came three times, and Zedekiah tries to escape but is caught in the plains of Jericho, then is taken to the king of Babylon at Riblah, “where he gave judgment upon him.”
The city is destroyed, the city is annihilated, and thousands of Jews are taken out of their homeland. Habakkuk was left in the homeland because he was poor; he was a poor prophet.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: Look at the judgment that happened to Zedekiah. The king of Babylon “slew the sons of Zedekiah” “before his eyes”: he killed his sons right in front of his face. He “slew all the nobles of Judah.” Then he “put out Zedekiah’s eyes”, took out his eyes, and “bound him with chains, to carry him to Babylon.” That was the judgment.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

points: The Chaldeans “burned the king’s house, and the houses of the people, with fire, and brake down the walls of Jerusalem.” This was the final judgment. This is what Jeremiah warned Zedekiah of, but the people would not listen. It is the same message we tell our people today, and they don’t want to listen. Babylon annihilated our people, and Babylon the Great annihilated our people: America, during slavery.

Toward the ending chapters of Jeremiah, chapters 45 through 51, come the prophecies against each country: Moab’s judgment, Ammon’s judgment, Egypt’s judgment, Damascus’ judgment, the judgment that came on the countries surrounding Israel. God used Nebuchadnezzar to bring judgment to those countries, and some of those prophecies have a double meaning.
